title: Universal closedness descends under fpqc scheme coverings for algebraic spaces
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism. Let $\{g_i:T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering by schemes [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], and write $f_i:X\times_TT_i\to T_i$ for the projections [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Universal closedness has the meaning of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]: after every algebraic-space base change, the induced map on field-valued point spaces with their atlas topology is closed. If every $f_i$ is universally closed, then $f$ is universally closed. No quasi-compactness, separatedness, finite-type, finite-presentation, flatness or Noetherian assumption on $f$ is made.

source.place: Tag 041O, lemma-descending-property-universally-closed, descent implication for a scheme target and a covering by schemes.

proof.text: All point maps of algebraic-space morphisms are continuous: for a morphism $v:A\to B$ and each representable etale scheme map $a:V\to A$, the composite $va:V\to B$ is continuous by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. The final-topology criterion of [def-a1-space-point-topology] therefore makes $|v|$ continuous. In particular, inverse images of closed subsets along all projections used below are closed.

source.place: Tag 03BX, lemma-topology-points (2), using the final topology of etale scheme maps.

proof.text: We will use the following elementary image calculation. For $p:E\to Z$ between algebraic spaces, a scheme map $a:U\to Z$, and any subset $C\subseteq|E|$, put $E_U=E\times_ZU$, with projections $r:E_U\to E$ and $p_U:E_U\to U$. The fibre product exists by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Then $a^{-1}(p(C))=p_U(r^{-1}(C))$. One inclusion follows from commutativity. For the reverse inclusion, take $u\in|U|$ and $e\in C$ with $a(u)=p(e)$. Choose a field-valued representative $\operatorname{Spec}K\to E$ of $e$. Apply [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point] with target $Z$ and scheme sources $\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $U$: it gives a point of $\operatorname{Spec}K\times_ZU$ over $u$. Its image in $E_U$ projects to $e$ and $u$, proving the assertion. This uses that lemma only with two scheme sources, exactly as stated.

source.place: Tag 03H4, lemma-points-cartesian; scheme-source specialization followed by the fibre-product universal property.

proof.text: Let $Z\to T$ be any algebraic-space morphism and $p:E=X\times_TZ\to Z$. Fix a closed subset $C\subseteq|E|$. For each representable etale scheme map $a:U\to Z$, set $U_i=U\times_TT_i$ and $q_i:U_i\to U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms](3), these scheme maps form an fpqc covering. Set $E_U=X\times_TU$ and $E_i=X\times_TU_i$, and let $C_U$ and $C_i$ be the inverse images of $C$ under the projections to $E$. They are closed by step 1. The fibre-product universal property in [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies $E_i\to U_i$ with the base change of $f_i$ along $U_i\to T_i$. Thus it is closed by the assumed universal closedness of $f_i$ and [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Write $A_U=p_U(C_U)$. Step 2 gives $q_i^{-1}(A_U)=p_i(C_i)$, so all these inverse images are closed.

The closedness of these inverse images implies that $A_U$ is closed, as follows. Give $D=\{0,1\}$ the topology $\{\varnothing,\{0\},D\}$ and let $\chi:|U|\to D$ be $1$ on $A_U$ and $0$ elsewhere. Each $\chi\circ q_i$ is continuous, since the inverse image of the sole nontrivial open $\{0\}$ is the complement of the closed set $q_i^{-1}(A_U)$. These functions agree on $U_i\times_UU_j$, because both are the same set function $\chi$ composed with its map to $U$. Apply [lem-sfb-set-continuous-functions-fpqc-sheaf] with this $D$ to glue them to a continuous $h:|U|\to D$. The maps $q_i$ are jointly surjective by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], so $h=\chi$ pointwise. Hence $|U|\setminus A_U=\chi^{-1}(\{0\})$ is open and $A_U$ is closed. This requires no separation property of $D$ and no quasi-compactness of the individual $q_i$.

source.place: Tag 041O, quotient-topology inference, implemented for a covering family by the elementary Sierpinski-space specialization of the cited continuous-map sheaf theorem.

proof.text: Step 2 also gives $a^{-1}(p(C))=A_U$ for every representable etale scheme map $a:U\to Z$. By step 4 these subsets are closed. Taking complements in the final-topology criterion [def-a1-space-point-topology] shows that $p(C)$ is closed in $|Z|$. Thus $p$ is a closed map. Since $Z\to T$ was an arbitrary algebraic-space base change and $C$ was an arbitrary closed subset, [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] gives universal closedness of $f$.

Step 1: the affine-étale-cover lemma gives continuity for every scheme-to-space map, and the final topology then gives continuity of |v|. Step 2: the point lemma, which allows only scheme sources, is applied with the scheme sources Spec K→E→Z and U→Z; the reverse inclusion of a^{-1}(p(C))=p_U(r^{-1}(C)) is checked. Step 3: {U×_T T_i→U} is fpqc by 022D(3); E_i→U_i is the base change of f_i along U_i→T_i, so it is closed; q_i^{-1}(A_U)=p_i(C_i). Step 4: the Mathlib leaf allows any topological target (no T2), so the Sierpiński gluing works; the family is compatible and joint surjectivity gives h=χ, so A_U is closed. Step 5: the final topology gives p(C) closed. Edge cases checked: empty index set (T empty), empty X and C, covering maps that are not quasi-compact. No new nodes.
